source.text_it: L'impresa di trasporto non è responsabile per le violazioni alla normativa in materia di tempi di guida e di riposo commesse, durante il lavoro, dai conducenti alle proprie dipendenze quando sono all'estero

records.localized_text: A transport company is not responsible for driving and rest time violations committed during work by its drivers when abroad.

source.text_it: Il regolamento 561/2006/CE prevede che, al fine di salvaguardare la sicurezza delle persone e delle cose trasportate, il conducente possa superare i tempi massimi di guida prescritti solo per raggiungere un luogo di sosta appropriato

records.localized_text: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 provides that, to safeguard the safety of persons and goods carried, a driver may exceed prescribed maximum driving times only to reach a suitable stopping place.

source.text_it: Il conducente che deroga alla durata massima della guida al fine di raggiungere un luogo di sosta appropriato, deve annotarne i motivi sul foglio di registrazione o sul retro della stampa giornaliera (ticket)

records.localized_text: A driver who departs from maximum driving time to reach a suitable stopping place must record the reasons on the record sheet or on the back of the daily printout.

source.text_it: Il regolamento 561/2006/CE prevede che il conducente possa superare i tempi massimi di guida prescritti per raggiungere il proprio domicilio

records.localized_text: Regulation (EC) No 561/2006 provides that a driver may exceed prescribed maximum driving times to reach their home.

source.text_it: Il regolamento 561/2006/CE prevede che il conducente possa superare i tempi massimi di guida prescritti per raggiungere il deposito dell'impresa proprietaria del veicolo

source.text_it: Secondo il regolamento 561/2006/CE, per "interruzione" si intende ogni periodo in cui il conducente non può guidare o svolgere altre mansioni

records.localized_text: Under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, a “break” means any period during which a driver may not drive or perform other work.

records.localized_text: Under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, “availability time” includes waiting at the workplace and multi-manning.

records.localized_text: Under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, daily rest may be split into two parts, the first at least 9 hours and the second at least 3 hours.

records.localized_text: Under Regulation (EC) No 561/2006, multi-manning applies when two drivers are on board throughout the period, except for the first three hours when the second driver's presence is optional.

rows.text: The undertaking may also be liable for infringements committed by its drivers in another country; national law may make liability subject to conditions.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 10(3), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — responsabilità dell’impresa anche per infrazioni all’estero, con possibili condizioni nazionali.

rows.text: To safeguard people, the vehicle or its load, a driver may depart from the limits only as necessary to reach a suitable stopping place, without jeopardising road safety. Article 12 separately allows a conditional exceptional return to the driver’s residence or employer’s operational centre for weekly rest.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006, article 12, consolidated from 20 August 2020: safety-to-suitable-stop provision; separately, exceptional return to residence or employer operational centre for weekly rest, up to one hour or up to two for regular weekly rest after immediately preceding uninterrupted 30-minute break; record reason and compensate extension en bloc by end of third following week. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2020-08-20

European Commission, Driving & rest times, Article 12 guidance: the 90-hour fortnightly driving limit and applicable six-24-hour weekly-rest deadline are not waived by the exceptional return derogation. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/road/mobility-package-i/driving-rest-times_en

Official superiori PDF, page 43 zero-based, prints 27585 VERO and 27587/27588 FALSO. Reading the latter as unconditional everyday permission is editorial interpretation, not a verified official explanation; the separate 2020 exceptional return derogation remains available subject to its conditions.

rows.text: To depart from the limits to reach a suitable stopping place, the driver must manually record the reason on the record sheet or printout by arrival there.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 12, primo comma, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — annotazione della ragione entro l’arrivo alla sosta adeguata.

rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: going home does not normally permit exceeding the limits. In exceptional circumstances, without jeopardising road safety, Article 12 permits return to the driver’s residence or employer’s operational centre for weekly rest: up to one extra hour, or two for regular weekly rest after an uninterrupted 30-minute break immediately before the extra driving. The reason must be recorded and the extension compensated by the end of the third following week.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006, article 12, consolidated from 20 August 2020: safety-to-suitable-stop provision; separately, exceptional return to residence or employer operational centre for weekly rest, up to one hour or up to two for regular weekly rest after immediately preceding uninterrupted 30-minute break; record reason and compensate extension en bloc by end of third following week. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2020-08-20

European Commission, Driving & rest times, Article 12 guidance: the 90-hour fortnightly driving limit and applicable six-24-hour weekly-rest deadline are not waived by the exceptional return derogation. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/road/mobility-package-i/driving-rest-times_en

Official superiori PDF, page 43 zero-based, prints 27585 VERO and 27587/27588 FALSO. rows.text: The quiz marks this FALSE: reaching the vehicle owner’s depot does not normally permit exceeding the limits. In exceptional circumstances, without jeopardising road safety, Article 12 permits return to the driver’s residence or employer’s operational centre for weekly rest, not just any owner’s depot: up to one extra hour, or two for regular weekly rest after an uninterrupted 30-minute break immediately before the extra driving. The reason must be recorded and the extension compensated by the end of the third following week.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006, article 12, consolidated from 20 August 2020: safety-to-suitable-stop provision; separately, exceptional return to residence or employer operational centre for weekly rest, up to one hour or up to two for regular weekly rest after immediately preceding uninterrupted 30-minute break; record reason and compensate extension en bloc by end of third following week. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2020-08-20

rows.text: A break is used exclusively for recuperation: the driver neither drives nor does other work during it.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(d), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — interruzione senza guida o altre mansioni e destinata al recupero.

rows.text: Rest is an uninterrupted period during which the driver can freely dispose of their time, without remaining available for work.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(f), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo ininterrotto con tempo liberamente disponibile.

rows.text: Availability is neither a break nor actual work: it includes foreseeable waiting periods under the prescribed conditions and, in multi-manning, time beside the driver or on a bunk while the vehicle is moving. Not every wait at the workplace is availability.
evidence: Direttiva 2002/15/CE, art. 3(a)-(b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32002L0015 — disponibilità distinta dal lavoro e dalle pause; attese prevedibili e tempo in multipresenza alle condizioni indicate.

rows.text: A stop is not automatically a break: a break must be devoted exclusively to recuperation, without driving or other work.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(d), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — interruzione destinata esclusivamente al recupero.

rows.text: Availability does not mean agreeing to work overtime: it is a period distinct from breaks and rest when the worker is ready to respond to a call, under the prescribed conditions.
evidence: Direttiva 2002/15/CE, art. 3(a)-(b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/ALL/?uri=CELEX:32002L0015 — disponibilità distinta dal lavoro e dalle pause; attese prevedibili e tempo in multipresenza alle condizioni indicate.

rows.text: The ordinary weekly driving limit is 56 hours; the limit of 90 hours in two consecutive weeks also applies.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 6(2)-(3), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — limiti di 56 ore settimanali e 90 in due settimane.

rows.text: The ordinary weekly driving limit is 56 hours; the maximum over two consecutive weeks is 90 hours. The exceptional return derogation for reaching the driver’s residence or employer’s operational centre can extend the weekly limit under its conditions, but not the 90-hour limit.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006, Article 6(2)–(3), ordinary weekly and fortnightly driving limits; Article 12, conditional exceptional extension. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2020-08-20

European Commission, Article 12 guidance: the exceptional return derogation does not waive the 90-hour fortnightly limit. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/road/mobility-package-i/driving-rest-times_en

rows.text: Split regular daily rest requires at least 3 consecutive hours first and at least 9 consecutive hours afterwards.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(g), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo giornaliero regolare frazionato: 3 ore poi 9.

rows.text: Regular weekly rest is at least 45 hours. It must normally begin within six 24-hour periods after the end of the previous weekly rest; reduced rest is also allowed under legal conditions.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(h), 8(6), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo regolare di almeno 45 ore, termine di sei periodi di 24 ore e riposo ridotto.

rows.text: Reduced weekly rest lasts at least 24 hours; the reduction must be compensated in one block by the end of the third following week, subject to the other weekly rest conditions.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(h), 8(6), 8(6b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo ridotto almeno 24 ore e compensazione entro la terza settimana successiva.

rows.text: In multi-manning at least two drivers must be available on board during the driving period concerned; only in the first hour is the second driver optional.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(o), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — multipresenza e prima ora facoltativa.

rows.text: The order is reversed: split regular daily rest starts with at least 3 consecutive hours, followed by at least 9.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(g), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo frazionato: 3 ore poi 9.

rows.text: The ordinary rule does not require 48 hours after four driving periods: regular weekly rest is at least 45 hours and normally starts within six 24-hour periods after the previous weekly rest.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(h), 8(6), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — riposo regolare di almeno 45 ore e termine ordinario di sei periodi di 24 ore.

rows.text: The second driver is optional only during the first hour of multi-manning, not the first three.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 4(o), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — secondo conducente facoltativo solo nella prima ora.

rows.text: The ordinary weekly driving limit is 56 hours, not 48; the 90-hour limit over two consecutive weeks also applies.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 6(2)-(3), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — 56 ore settimanali e 90 in due settimane.

rows.text: The ordinary weekly limit is 56 hours, but the maximum over two consecutive weeks is 90 hours, not 100. The exceptional return derogation for reaching the driver’s residence or employer’s operational centre can extend the weekly limit under its conditions, but not the 90-hour limit.
evidence: Regulation (EC) 561/2006, Article 6(2)–(3), ordinary weekly and fortnightly driving limits; Article 12, conditional exceptional extension. https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2020-08-20

European Commission, Article 12 guidance: the exceptional return derogation does not waive the 90-hour fortnightly limit. https://transport.ec.europa.eu/transport-modes/road/mobility-package-i/driving-rest-times_en

rows.text: After 4½ hours of driving a break of at least 45 minutes is required unless a rest period begins; the break may also be split under the prescribed conditions.
evidence: Regolamento (CE) 561/2006, art. 7, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf — interruzione di 45 minuti dopo 4 ore e mezza, salvo riposo, con frazionamento ammesso.

rows.text: The circular steering-wheel-like symbol identifies driving time on the tachograph.
evidence: Regolamento (UE) 165/2014, art. 34(5)(b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R0165 — pittogrammi distinti per guida, disponibilità e riposo.

rows.text: The bed symbol identifies breaks and rest periods on the tachograph.
evidence: Regolamento (UE) 165/2014, art. 34(5)(b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R0165 — pittogrammi distinti per guida, disponibilità e riposo.

rows.text: The square crossed by a diagonal identifies availability on the tachograph.
evidence: Regolamento (UE) 165/2014, art. 34(5)(b), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32014R0165 — pittogrammi distinti per guida, disponibilità e riposo.

issues.reason: Il quesito afferma che, per la sicurezza delle persone e cose trasportate, il superamento è consentito solo per raggiungere una sosta appropriata; la formulazione esclusiva è in conflitto con la deroga aggiuntiva per il rientro introdotta nel 2020. Il verdetto stampato è VERO e occorre adjudicare la portata di “solo” nel quesito.
checked_sources: Regolamento 561/2006, art. 12, primo, secondo e terzo comma, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf: la sosta appropriata è una deroga; esiste anche una distinta deroga eccezionale per raggiungere domicilio o sede operativa.
Regolamento (UE) 2020/1054, art. 1(11), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32020R1054: aggiunge le deroghe per il rientro.

issues.reason: Il quesito dichiara FALSO che si possa superare il tempo massimo per raggiungere il proprio domicilio; l’art. 12 vigente lo consente a condizioni eccezionali specifiche. Serve adjudicazione del conflitto con il verdetto stampato.
checked_sources: Regolamento 561/2006, art. 12, secondo e terzo comma, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf: consente aumenti limitati della guida giornaliera e settimanale per raggiungere il domicilio e fare il riposo settimanale, alle condizioni previste.
Regolamento (UE) 2020/1054, art. 1(11), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32020R1054: ha introdotto questa deroga.

issues.reason: Il quesito dichiara FALSO che si possa superare il massimo per raggiungere il deposito dell’impresa proprietaria; l’attuale deroga consente il rientro alla sede operativa del datore di lavoro a condizioni specifiche. Non è chiarito se il deposito indicato coincida con tale sede: serve adjudicazione della formulazione e del verdetto stampato.
checked_sources: Regolamento 561/2006, art. 12, secondo e terzo comma, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2006/561/2024-05-22/eng/pdf: deroga eccezionale limitata per raggiungere la sede operativa del datore di lavoro per il riposo settimanale.
Regolamento (UE) 2020/1054, art. 1(11), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/PDF/?uri=CELEX:32020R1054: ha introdotto la deroga.

issues: 27595, 27604: The explanations assert the 56-hour weekly driving limit without qualifying the exceptional article 12 extension, although 27587/27588 explain that extension correctly. Describe 56 hours as the ordinary weekly limit while retaining the 90-hour maximum over two consecutive weeks.

prior_review_findings.author: gpt-6.1-terra / collaboration /root/terra_runner
issues: 27595, 27604: The learner text asserts that Article 12 as a whole does not waive the 90-hour limit. The Commission guidance establishes this for the exceptional return derogation, but Article 12 first paragraph separately permits departure from Articles 6–9, as necessary to reach a suitable stopping place for safety; this includes Article 6(3). Restrict the 90-hour statement to the return derogation.
